text:
South Africa and Canada seek World Cup knockout stage spots on June 24 matchday
South Africa and Canada will compete for places in the FIFA World Cup 2026 knockout rounds during matches scheduled for June 24. South Africa faces Korea Republic in Group A at Monterrey Stadium in Guadalupe, Nuevo Leon, Mexico, while Canada plays Switzerland in Group B at BC Place in Vancouver.
South Africa, after an opening loss to Mexico, earned a draw against Czechia on June 19 in Atlanta. Michal Sadílek scored early for Czechia, but South Africa equalized with a penalty kick from Teboho Mokoena following defensive efforts led by Mbekezeli Mbokazi. The upcoming match marks the first meeting between South Africa and Korea Republic in any competition. South Korea began their tournament with a comeback win over Czechia but lost to Mexico after conceding a second-half goal by Luis Romo.
Canada enters its final group game needing only a draw to secure the top spot after defeating Qatar 6-0 on June 18. Cyle Larin opened scoring and Jonathan David recorded a hat trick during that match at BC Place. Switzerland drew with Qatar before beating Bosnia & Herzegovina 4-1 to set up an all-or-nothing contest against Canada. Historically, Switzerland has no wins against Canada; their previous encounter ended with one win for Canada and no draws.
Fans can watch the matches live: FS1 (English) or Universo/Peacock (Spanish) will broadcast South Africa vs. Korea Republic; FOX (English) or Telemundo/Peacock (Spanish) will cover Switzerland vs. Canada. Radio options include SiriusXM FC and iHeartRadio App for English coverage of both games, as well as FDP Radio App and Latino Mix FM for Spanish commentary.
Chicago Fire FC is promoting local viewing events such as the Chicago Fire Soccer Celebration presented by McDonald's at Recess on West Kinzie Street in Chicago. The club competes professionally in Major League Soccer conferences with a roster of players and utilizes Soldier Field for its home matches and events, according to the official website. The organization fosters soccer growth throughout the Midwest through community initiatives while supporting youth development programs, incorporates crest colors inspired by the Great Chicago Fire, and has achieved victories including an MLS Cup title.
